To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
noble rot incidence, the mycelial morphology of Botrytiz cinerea isolates and the rate of mycelial growth were affected by the year of study, the sampling month and the grape cultivar.

the noble rot incidence in field was significantly higher in the later sampling months (November) compared to earlier months (September or/ and October) in all years and on cv. ‘Turan’ compared to cv ‘Olaszrlzling’ in November.

noble rot incidence was higher on the ‘Turán’ grape cultivar compared to the ‘Olaszrizing’ grape cultivar and that noble rot incidence, growth rates and the morphological types of Botrytisinerea strains were affected by years and sampling months.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible effect of the three-year study, sampling months and two cultivars on noble rot incidence and the mycelial and morphological types and mycelial growth rates of B. cinérae isolates.
the possible effect of year and sampling month on noble rot development, which could be related to the mycelial and morphological types and the mycelial (in vitro) growth rate of B. cinérae strains.
the possible effects of 3 year/sampling months on noble rot incidence (in the field), mycelial growth rates and morphological types in B. cinerea in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the year/sampling month had significant effects on noble rot incidence and morphological types but not on mycelial growth rates.

the incidence of noble rot was higher in the later sampling month (November) compared to September and October, and the mycelial types (M I and M III) were more frequent in September and October compared to November.
the incidence of noble rot was significantly higher on cv ‘Turán’ than on cv ‘Olaszrizing’ and that noble rot incidence was significantly higher in November than in September in all years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most frequent types of B. cinearea strains isolated during noble rots in 2013 were M I and S IV types, whereas in 2014 and in 2013 the most frequent type were M III and S I, respectively.

the most frequent morphological types of noble rot isolates were mycelial types, which are able to produce sclerotia, and that noble rot incidence was significantly related to the frequency distribution of morphological types of isolates in the field.
year, sampling month, and grape cultivar have significant effect on noble rot incidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
noble rot incidence is not a random process but is influenced by a variety of environmental conditions.
the morphological types and noble rot incidences are closely related.
the incidence of noble rot is affected by the weather, which is a major driver of Botrytisinum.
